title: Onboarding: Role-Based Cohort Sprint Playbook (30/60/90)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a pragmatic, role-based 30/60/90 onboarding plan designed for compact cohort sprints. It focuses on measurable time-to-value for teams integrating Redwood Inference (hosted, dedicated, or private) and signals that indicate momentum toward renewal. The doc is intentionally operational — checklists, sample outreach copy, dashboard KPIs, and small experiments to run during weeks 1–12.

Who this is for:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs) running mid-market and enterprise onboarding
- Solutions Engineers supporting technical integration
- Customer platform/infra owners (DevOps/Platform) who will manage Dedicated/Private deployments

Primary success objective (30/60/90):
- 30 days: Integration baseline — customer has a reproducible end-to-end call to the Redwood API (or deployed private endpoint) with basic monitoring and one smoke test scenario producing expected outputs.
- 60 days: Productized flow — at least one LLM-backed feature in a low-risk surface (internal tool, staging environment, or beta release), basic performance targets (p50 latency, error rate) met, and cost per-token estimate validated.
- 90 days: Business impact — feature is in production or scheduled for GA, usage patterns established, runway-to-renewal signals captured (adoption, DAU/MAU, session length, API key usage), and an initial renewal health score created.

Role-based tracks (parallel workstreams):
- Developer/Engineer track: API integration, tracing, autoscaling knobs, E2E test harness, and perf regression checks.
- Platform/SRE track: VPC routing (if Private), HSM/KMS setup, capacity sizing for Dedicated, alerting thresholds.
- Product/PM track: Define success scenarios, prompt set for quality validation, UX guardrails, rollout policy (canary/A-B/fallback).
- Business/Stakeholder track: Value metrics, cadence for check-ins, internal adoption champions, and renewal owner identified.

Week-by-week sprint checklist (compact cohort version):
Weeks 0–1 (Pre-kick/Day 0):
- Kickoff call scheduled: agenda includes roles, test cases, security questions, and a decision on deployment mode.
- Provisioning: API key created or Private control-plane access granted; basic network allowlists configured.
- Quick wins list: 3 measurable smoke tests (e.g., paraphrase rewriting, summarization of a sampled doc, a simple search-rewrite loop).
- Owner: CSM + SE.

Weeks 2–4 (30-day goal):
- Integration: App calls Redwood API or local endpoint with end-to-end traces captured (X-Request-Id or similar).
- Logging/Observability: Token-level cost and p50/p95 latency visible in a dashboard.
- Quality check: Run defined prompt set against baseline model variant; capture acceptance criteria pass/fail.
- Security signoff path documented (who approves) and any PII handling noted.
- Stakeholder touch: 30-min design review demo.

Weeks 5–8 (60-day goal):
- Feature rollout: First feature behind feature flag in a target environment.
- Performance tuning: Apply batching/caching suggestions, try one quantization profile if cost reduction is required.
- Scale test: Synthetic load test to estimated peak concurrency.
- Eval: Collect human-reviewed samples and surface quality regressions; link to Redwood Optimize recommendations.
- Stakeholder touch: 1-hour adoption planning with success metrics defined.

Weeks 9–12 (90-day goal):
- Production readiness: Finalize runbooks, escalation path, and SLA expectations.
- Adoption: Measure early adopter cohort behavior and start a small rollout plan.
- Renewal signals: Build simple renewal health dashboard with weighted signals (usage velocity, error rate, qualitative sentiment).
- Closeout: Executive summary delivered, ask for NPS/feedback.

Measurable KPIs and thresholds (examples to preconfigure in dashboards):
- Integration KPI: completed E2E API call with tracing within 7 days of kickoff.
- Reliability KPI: p95 latency <= target (customer-specific, default target: 800ms for chat-like flows), error rate < 1% over a 24-hour window.
- Cost KPI: estimated cost-per-1k tokens agreed and < X% over project budget (X negotiated).
- Adoption KPI: baseline DAU/MAU for the feature, activation rate of invited users, 2–3 power users actively using the feature by day 60.
- Quality KPI: pass rate on the agreed prompt set >= 80% or improvement plan defined.

Renewal health score (simple weighted signals):
- Usage velocity (40%): 30/60/90 growth vs baseline.
- Reliability/Errors (20%): inversely weighted by incidents.
- Cost alignment (15%): within budget.
- Qualitative sentiment (15%): feedback from product owners.
- Roadmap alignment (10%): planned feature dependencies satisfied.

Red flags to escalate immediately:
- No E2E call within 10 business days.
- Repeated performance regressions blocking feature rollout.
- Unresolved network/security gating preventing test traffic.

Risk ledger (quick template rows to track):
- Risk title | Owner | Impact (H/M/L) | Mitigation | Status | Notes
- Example: KMS integration delays | Platform Owner | H | Temporary key with narrower scope; follow weekly KMS runbook | Open | ETA 2 weeks

Small experiments to run during the cohort (1–2 week experiments):
- Prompt pruning: measure latency and cost delta after removing non-essential prompt context.
- Batching A/B: compare single-request latency vs micro-batching at low concurrency to see cost tradeoffs.
- Model variant fallback: test routing policy to a smaller quantized model and validate quality drop.

Communications & meeting cadence (recommended):
- Weekly tactical sync (30 mins) weeks 0–8: CSM + SE + Platform rep.
- Biweekly stakeholder review (45 mins) weeks 4–12: product owner + engineering manager.
- Ad-hoc Incident channel in Slack (create #cs-<customer>-onboard).
- Shared drive folder for artifacts and runbooks.

Sample outreach templates (short):
- Kickoff invite subject: "[Customer] x Redwood — Onboarding kickstart (30/60/90 plan)"
  Body (short): "Hi <Name>, excited to kick off. Agenda: integration checkpoints, security needs, and success metrics. Please confirm attendees and any high-priority test cases. — Aisha (CSM)"

- 30-day check-in subject: "30-day integration status + quick demo"
  Body (short): "We have an E2E smoke test passing. Attached: traces and baseline metrics. Next: performance tuning and feature flag rollout. Can we schedule 30 mins next week to align?"

- 60-day adoption note subject: "60-day: feature beta ready — adoption plan"
  Body (short): "Feature is behind a flag in staging. Proposed pilot group: X users. KPIs to monitor: latency, error rate, token cost, and feature activation. Seeking approval to expand to 10 pilot users."

Handoff checklist for renewal owner (at 60–90 days):
- Confirm renewal owner and decision timeline.
- Populate renewal health dashboard and attach evidence for each signal.
- Document expected usage growth and projected committed spend.
- Attach any unresolved risks and mitigation timelines.

Operational templates to attach to the shared folder (action items):
- Prompt set CSV (20 canonical prompts for eval).
- Smoke test script (curl examples and SDK snippets).
- Runbook: incident, rollback, and canary rollback steps.
- Simple dashboard json or dashboard spec to import to common tooling (Datadog/Grafana).

Notes & considerations specific to Redwood Inference customers:
- Choose routing policy early (latency-first vs cost-first) — this informs which model variants and Dedicated sizing to prefer.
- Leverage Redwood Optimize recommendations after day 30 — quick wins often come from batching/cache policies and trying a single quantized variant.
- For Private deployments, prioritize network egress test early; many delays stem from firewall rules and certificate provisioning.

Next steps (CSM owner):
1) Share this playbook in kickoff folder and confirm attendees.
2) Drop initial prompt set and smoke tests into the shared folder within 48 hours.
3) Run pre-kick check: API key, allowlist, and initial sample doc.

Appendix: minimal dashboard spec (fields to show) — useful to ask customer to share or to configure during onboarding:
- API calls per minute (last 24h)
- Token consumption per route (24h)
- p50/p95 latency per route (24h)
- Error rate % per route (24h)
- Cost per 1k tokens (rolling 7d)
- Top prompt failures and sample request ids

Document history:
- 2025-08-12 created by Aisha Patel (initial draft)
- 2025-08-22 updated: added role tracks and experiments (Marco R.)
- 2025-09-02 updated: clarified renewal signals and sample outreach (Lena C.)

Open questions for product/solutions:
- Should we include a canned Datadog dashboard export or a Grafana JSON by default?
- Any preferred default thresholds for p95 latency per product vertical?

End of playbook.
